page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.s6-c1m4.2xlarge is an entry-level virtual server instance belonging to the shared instance family. It is provisioned on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance delivers 8 virtual CPUs paired with 32.0 GB of memory, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM balance with 4.0 GB of memory allocated per core.

Operating with a shared CPU allocation model, the instance shares physical host compute resources with other tenant workloads rather than dedicating physical CPU cores. This architecture presents a cost-efficient resource profile for systems requiring high memory capacity and multiple vCPUs without the overhead of enterprise dedicated instances. However, compute throughput can experience variability based on multi-tenant host activity, making it unsuitable for sustained, latency-sensitive compute tasks.

Storage and network configurations are structured around external cloud infrastructure, as the server provides no integrated local disk storage. All persistent data requires external network block storage. Networking capability includes a 1 Gbps baseline bandwidth, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses assigned by default. Hardware accelerators such as GPUs are not present.

Due to the shared processor allocation and lack of local NVMe storage, the ecs.s6-c1m4.2xlarge is appropriate for general-purpose workloads with moderate or intermittent CPU demands. Common deployment targets include non-critical web applications, staging environments, internal development portals, asynchronous background processing workers, and small databases where workload variance is tolerated.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.s6-c1m4.2xlarge is a shared-core general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture and managed by the KVM hypervisor. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz, the configuration supplies 8 shared vCPUs and 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced 1:4 ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The server includes no integrated local storage, requiring network-attached block volumes for system and user data, while network throughput is defined by a 1 Gbps baseline bandwidth with no complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Because the compute resources use a shared allocation model, execution throughput may exhibit variability under multi-tenant host load, trading sustained deterministic processing for a budget-friendly resource density. This setup is suited for cost-sensitive general-purpose environments, such as development clusters, low-traffic web applications, non-critical background jobs, and test staging environments.
